event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: Only one passage in CME’s 2023 Form 10-K explicitly references pandemic exposure.  It places pandemics alongside a long list of exogenous factors that can dampen or shift trading volumes.  The wording is purely generic—there is no reference to COVID-19 by name, no quantified effect, and no description of supply-chain, labour, technology or demand shocks.  The company therefore frames pandemic danger as a broad, forward-looking contingency rather than as an active, measured headwind.  Because the filing date (Feb 2024) is just under four years after the WHO’s March 2020 declaration, the Time-Decay Principle permits only a mid-range score if the disclosure were strong; however, the abstract nature of the language materially downgrades the severity.  Overall, the evidence supports a low-to-moderate risk score: the risk is acknowledged but not detailed or monetised, suggesting limited residual concern to investors at this point.

evidence_list.snippet: • pandemics affecting our customer base or our ability to operate our markets;

components.reason: Explicitly identifies pandemics as a potential threat to both customers and the firm’s operational continuity (direct risk acknowledgement).
Presented as an unquantified, catch-all bullet within a longer list—no specific reference to COVID-19 impacts, financial magnitude, or mitigation.
Falls within ~4 years of the event onset; Time-Decay permits a moderate weighting.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: The sentence clearly flags pandemic exposure but does so generically and without data; after time-decay adjustment the net severity is low-moderate (3/10).
